cells.tense: You can let one thing end here without forcing the next to reveal itself.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Take one feeling about the ending and settle what it's owed — rest, a walk, an hour of nothing — then give it exactly that. Nobody else weighs in on the call.
cells.core:
You can end something here without needing the next thing to show up first. In a stretch where only the next step is lit, what's finished gets let go cleanly, and the ground for what comes is usually made that way — the ending does most of the work. Something in you is doing this carefully, and it isn't the forced kind.

Fairness toward your own feeling is where this grows next: settled while the fog is still fog. Take one feeling about the ending — relief, grief, plain tiredness — and work out what it's owed. Rest, a walk, an hour of nothing. Then give it exactly that, and keep the call yours alone. Stay with a feeling you can name without straining.

cells.verb: composting what's finished into ground where something new can grow

cells.tense: You will have ended it and rebuilt it before anything shows you what it was.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: When someone near the ending feels something, stay with them and leave it unfixed — no explaining, no improving, no making it better. Then carry on as usual.
cells.core:
Endings are being made ahead of what they hold — in what you share and in what you carry alone. Each one looks obvious from where you stand, and the fog clears fast when the scythe is in your hands. What's thin here is sitting inside the unfinished thing long enough to feel what it still carries for the person across from you.

That's small enough to practice. When someone near the ending feels something, stay with them and leave it unfixed — no explaining, no improving, no making it better. Then carry on. You'll find the next ending is smaller and less necessary, and the person is still with you after it.

cells.tense: The ending already happened, and you have kept standing at the door it closed.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Go once this week to something you actually want to be part of. Don't schedule a second visit, don't set a pace — go on your own account.
cells.core:
Something already ended, and you're still inside where it used to be. The slot is empty, the practice isn't running, and the fog isn't the trouble. Keeping the old shape open is what stopped the renewal, not the loss. This stretch of life only ever shows one step. Waiting for more than that has been the stance sitting still.

Courage works from the inside out. Go once this week to something you actually want to be part of. Don't force a second visit, don't set a schedule. Feed it a little at a time. A foot lands somewhere new, the next stretch of light appears, and what ended stops being the place you live.

cells.tense: You are already letting the stale thing go, and you would say it happened by itself.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Choose a draining thing in the fog — not the biggest, a clear one — and put a boundary around it. Put it where you'll see it held.
cells.core:
You're already letting something end, in a stretch where only the next step is lit, and the one doing it is you. Ask and you'd say it happened by itself, or that nothing was decided. Something was decided. The ending is being written, just not signed, and the edge of it is what the others can feel.

What you started from is smaller: a line, drawn and kept. Choose a draining thing in the fog — not the biggest, a clear one — and put a boundary around it. Put it where you'll see it held. The unspoken thinning becomes a line with your name on it, and the change stops being something that happens to you.
